8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: Suwāʿ — the name of one of the ancient idols worshipped by the people of Nūḥ. It designates a particular object of false worship and carries no separate sense as an ordinary Arabic word.
9.grammar: A proper name that still takes full nunation (triptote), so its -an ending marks the accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb. No Arabic root can be securely assigned to it, which fits its being a borrowed or purely conventional name rather than a word derived from a living root.

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: Yaghūth — the name of one of the ancient idols worshipped by the people of Nūḥ. It names a particular object of false worship; the letters themselves have the shape of a verb meaning "he helps, he comes to the rescue".
11.grammar: A proper name of the diptote class: because it is shaped exactly like an imperfect verb ("he helps"), it refuses the -n of nunation and uses only two endings instead of three. The bare -a here is its accusative, the case used for the direct object of a verb; a diptote never shows -in and takes -a where other nouns would take -i.
11.root: غ-و-ث (gh-w-th) — to help, succour, come to the rescue

12.meaning: And Yaʿūq — the name of one of the ancient idols worshipped by the people of Nūḥ. The letters have the shape of a verb meaning "he hinders, he holds back", but as used the word is a name.
12.grammar: A proper name joined by wa- "and". Being built on the pattern of an imperfect verb ("he hinders"), it is a diptote — a name that refuses nunation and uses only two case endings — so the plain -a is its accusative, the case for the direct object of a verb, and it never takes -in or -i.
12.root: ع-و-ق (ʿ-w-q) — to hinder, hold back, obstruct

13.meaning: And Nasr — the name of one of the ancient idols worshipped by the people of Nūḥ. The same word as a common noun means a vulture or eagle, but as used it is a name.

parts.en: Nasr (name of an idol; also "vulture, eagle")

13.grammar: A name joined by wa- "and". It keeps full nunation (triptote), so the -an ending marks the accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb.
13.root: ن-س-ر (n-s-r) — the vulture/eagle; to tear or pluck at prey

1.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

2.meaning: They led astray, they caused others to go wrong. The base verb means to lose the way or wander off the right path; in this causative shape it means to make someone else lose it — to mislead.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb of Form IV, the causative pattern formed by the prefixed a-, turning "to stray" into "to make stray". The -ū ending says the doers are "they" (masculine plural) and that the action is completed; the alif written after it is silent.
2.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, err

3.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
3.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (the 'tanwīn' of fatḥa). The accusative case here commonly marks an object of a verb or an indefinite quantity; the doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the word is indefinite ('many', not 'the many').
3.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: You increase / add to. The verb means to give more of something, to augment or add on to what is already there.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking "you" (or a feminine "she") as the doer. Its mood is the jussive — the clipped form used after negating and prohibiting particles — whose stem normally ends in a vowelless consonant. The -i written and heard at the end is not a case or mood ending at all: it is a helping vowel supplied so that the vowelless final consonant does not collide with a consonant cluster beginning the next word.
5.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, add, grow more

6.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
6.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: straying / error — the state of being lost from the right path, wandering far from guidance and truth. A verbal noun naming the condition of going astray.
8.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the faʿāl pattern, naming the act/state of straying. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — often used for the object of a verb or as an absolute object reinforcing a verb ('to stray a [great] straying') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
8.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

1.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
1.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

2.meaning: Their sins, their wrongdoings, their offences — acts of moral error and transgression. The underlying word covers both mistake and deliberate fault, and in religious usage it means an act that misses the mark set by Allah.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural (marked by the -āt ending) of a noun meaning a sin or fault. This plural class has only two endings: -u for the subject case, and -i for everything else — both the direct-object case and the case that follows prepositions or links a noun to a following possessor ("… OF …"). The -i shown here is that second ending. The attached -him is the possessive pronoun "their" (masculine group); its vowel shifts from -hum to -him to harmonise with the preceding i.
2.root: خ-ط-ء (kh-ṭ-ʾ) — to err, miss the mark, do wrong

3.meaning: They were drowned — they were made to sink and perish in water. This is the passive of a causative verb, so the sense is that something outside them brought the drowning about.

parts.en: causative prefix carrying the passive vowel

3.grammar: Past-tense verb, Form IV (causative: "to drown someone"), put into the passive. Arabic marks the past passive purely by vowels — u on the first syllable and i before the last consonant — so the doer is left unnamed and the persons spoken of are the ones acted upon. The -ū ending shows they are "they" (masculine plural) and the action is completed; the written alif after it is silent.
3.root: غ-ر-ق (gh-r-q) — to sink, drown, be submerged

4.meaning: So/then they were made to enter — they were admitted or caused to go in. The causative of "to enter", in the passive, so entry is something done to them.

parts.en: causative prefix carrying the passive vowel

4.grammar: Past-tense Form IV (causative) verb in the passive, introduced by fa- "so/then", a connector implying that what follows comes as an immediate consequence of what preceded. The u-…-i- vowel pattern is what makes the past tense passive, leaving the agent unmentioned. The -ū ending marks the persons as "they" (masculine plural) with the action completed; the trailing alif is silent.

5.meaning: Fire — blazing flame; by extension heat, burning, or (in many contexts) the Fire of punishment. The core image is leaping, consuming flame.
5.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (the 'nunation' tanwīn). This ending commonly signals 'a fire' as the direct object of a verb, i.e. the thing acted upon.
5.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (نَار 'fire' is a derived noun from this root)

6.meaning: A two-part device meaning 'did not …' — it combines 'and/then so' with a negating word that turns a present-tense verb into a flat statement that something did NOT happen in the past.
6.grammar: A connecting particle fa- ('and so / then') joined to the negative particle lam. Lam negates the past: it precedes a present-tense verb but flips its meaning to 'did not do', and it puts that following verb into the jussive (clipped) form.

7.meaning: They find, come upon, perceive — the act of finding or discovering done by a group, presented as ongoing or as a possibility (not yet completed).
7.grammar: A present-tense verb, 'they find,' with the ya-…-ū frame marking a group of males/mixed as the doers. The absence of a final 'nūn' (it is -ū, not -ūna) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood — the verb is shortened because a preceding particle governs it (e.g., a negation or condition).
7.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon; to perceive, to feel

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
10.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
10.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: Helpers, supporters, defenders — those who come to someone's aid and stand with them against an adversary. The root joins the ideas of helping and of the victory that help brings.
12.grammar: A broken (internally reshaped) plural of nāṣir/naṣīr "helper". The -an ending marks it indefinite and accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb and for the noun governed by a negating expression such as "you will not find any …".
12.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, give victory

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: Nūḥ (Noah) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no general lexical meaning.
2.grammar: A proper noun in the nominative case, marked by the -un ending. The nominative typically identifies the doer/subject of a sentence or the thing being named.

3.meaning: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
3.grammar: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: To leave something alone, let it be, abandon or forsake it — to relinquish a thing and walk away from it rather than keep or maintain it. The verb is used almost exclusively in the present/future and command forms; its past-tense sense is supplied by another verb (taraka).

parts.en: you (one man) / she — the subject prefix

5.grammar: Present-tense (imperfect) verb, basic (Form I) pattern. The ta- prefix marks the doer as either 'you' (a single male addressee) or 'she'. The stem ends with no vowel at all (sukūn, hence '-dhar' not '-dharu'): that vowel-less ending is the jussive mood, the clipped form a verb takes after words that negate or command it — for example after lā ('do not…'), lam ('did not…'), or in the 'if…' half of a conditional sentence.
5.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — leaving off, forsaking, letting go

6.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
6.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
6.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
9.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

10.meaning: A single dweller, a solitary soul who inhabits or moves about a place. The form is emphatic, and it is used idiomatically in negative statements to mean 'not one living person', 'not a soul left in the land' — the emphatic minimum of habitation.

parts.en: one who dwells / goes about in a place; a single soul

10.grammar: A noun on the fayʿāl pattern built from a hollow root (one whose middle letter is the weak letter و). The expected *daywār* becomes dayyār by a standard sound rule: when a yāʾ and a wāw come together and the first of the two carries sukūn, the wāw turns into yāʾ and the pair merges into a doubled yy — the same change that gives sayyid from س-و-د and mayyit from م-و-ت. The doubling is therefore an effect of that weak-letter assimilation, not the doubled middle root letter of the intensive faʿʿāl pattern. The final '-an' is two things at once: the doubled vowel sign (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a/any', not 'the'), and the 'a' vowel is the accusative case, the ending a noun takes when it is the object of a verb, or is otherwise governed by a verb or by certain particles.
10.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — turning, circling round; a dwelling one revolves within

1.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
1.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: To leave them be, forsake them, let them alone — the act of relinquishing a group of people and abandoning them to their state, with the people themselves attached to the verb as its object.

parts.en: you (one man) / she — the subject prefix
them (a group of males or a mixed group)

3.grammar: Present-tense (imperfect) verb, basic (Form I) pattern, with an object pronoun attached to the end. The ta- prefix marks the doer as 'you' (a single male addressee) or 'she'. The verb stem carries no mood vowel before the pronoun (sukūn on the -r): that vowel-less ending is the jussive mood, the shortened form used after negating or commanding words such as lā ('do not…') and lam ('did not…'), and in 'if…' clauses. The '-hum' on the end is the receiver of the action — 'them'.
3.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — leaving off, forsaking, letting go

4.meaning: For them to lead others astray — to cause someone to lose the way, to misguide them off a straight path. The verb is in the causative pattern, marked by the 'u' vowel on its prefix: not 'to go astray' oneself but 'to make another go astray', whether by deceit, by false teaching, or by example. (The doubled l belongs to the root itself, whose second and third letters are the same, and appears equally in the plain non-causative verb ḍalla, 'he went astray'.)

parts.en: they/he (third person) — subject prefix, with the 'u' vowel that marks the causative pattern
they (a group of males or a mixed group)

4.grammar: Present-tense (imperfect) verb, causative (Form IV) pattern. The ya-/yu- prefix means the doer is third person ('he/they', not 'I' or 'you'), and the 'u' vowel on that prefix is the fingerprint of the causative pattern — 'cause to do'. The doubled l is a feature of the root, which is a geminate root (its last two letters identical), so the doubling carries no causative meaning of its own. The '-ū' ending means the doers are plural and male (or a mixed group). Note what is missing: the full plural ending is '-ūna', and the dropped final 'n' signals the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form a verb takes after words meaning 'that…', 'so that…', 'will not…', 'do not…', or in an 'if…' clause.
4.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — straying, losing the way, error

5.meaning: Servants / devoted worshippers belonging to 'you' (one person): human beings as those who serve and worship, here marked as 'your servants'. The word carries the sense of humble servitude and devotion.
5.grammar: A plural noun ('servants/worshippers') in a possessive construction with the attached -ka ('your', addressing one person). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the word as the object of a verb or governed by certain particles; attaching the pronoun makes the whole phrase definite ('your servants').

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: For them to beget, father, or give birth to offspring — to bring forth a child. The verb covers both the father's begetting and the mother's bearing, the general act of producing progeny.

parts.en: they (a group of males or a mixed group)

7.grammar: Present-tense (imperfect) verb, basic (Form I) pattern; the root's initial 'w' drops away in the present tense, leaving the bare '-lid-' stem. The ya- prefix means the doer is third person ('he/they'). The '-ū' ending means the doers are plural and male (or a mixed group). The full plural ending would be '-ūna'; the missing final 'n' marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the shortened form used after 'that…', 'so that…', 'will not…', 'do not…', or in an 'if…' clause.

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: One who is brazenly wicked — a person who breaks out of the bounds of right conduct and does so openly and shamelessly. The underlying image is of something bursting or splitting open, so a fājir is one who has ruptured the restraints of moral and religious limits rather than merely slipping.

parts.en: one who is wicked, immoral, brazenly transgressing

9.grammar: An active participle on the fāʿil pattern — a noun/adjective naming the one who performs the action, like English '-er' or '-ing one'. The final '-an' is doubly informative: the doubled vowel sign (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a wicked one', not 'the'), and the 'a' vowel is the accusative case, the ending used when the word is the object of a verb or otherwise governed by a verb or certain particles.
9.root: ف-ج-ر (f-j-r) — splitting/bursting open; hence breaking through moral bounds (and the daybreak breaking through night)

10.meaning: One who is deeply and persistently ungrateful or denying — an intensive form, so not simply 'a disbeliever' but one settled and unrelenting in covering over the truth and in refusing to acknowledge favour received. The root sense is 'to cover', so the word pictures someone burying what he knows to be true, and burying the kindness shown to him.

parts.en: utterly ungrateful one; hardened denier of truth

10.grammar: A noun/adjective in the intensive faʿʿāl pattern, formed by doubling the middle root letter (f), which magnifies the quality — 'much', 'repeatedly', 'thoroughly' so. The final '-an' carries two signals: the doubled vowel sign (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …'), and the 'a' vowel is the accusative case, the ending a noun takes as the object of a verb or when governed by a verb or certain particles.
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over, concealing; hence ingratitude and denial of truth

1.meaning: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
1.grammar: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

2.meaning: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
2.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

3.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
3.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

4.meaning: Parents — the two who gave one birth, father and mother taken together as a pair.
4.grammar: A dual noun ('the two parents') carrying the possessive 'my.' It follows the preposition li- ('for / to'). The dual ending appears in its genitive form -ay (rather than -ā), which is the shape duals take after a preposition or in a possession link; the attached -ya is 'my,' so the whole means 'and for my two parents.'

5.meaning: 'And for whoever / and to the one who' — combining 'and,' the preposition 'for/to,' and the relative word 'man' meaning 'whoever' or 'the one who,' used of persons.
5.grammar: Three particles joined together. 'wa' is 'and'; 'li-' is the preposition 'for/to'; 'man' is a relative/conditional pronoun meaning 'whoever' or 'the one who,' used only for people (as opposed to 'mā' for things). These words do not take case endings.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he entered' or 'he went in' — to pass into an enclosed place, a house, a state, or among a group.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he entered'. The final -a vowel is the standard ending of this verb pattern and signals a completed action by a single male subject.

7.meaning: My house, my dwelling. 'Bayt' (house/abode) with the first-person possessive, making it 'my house.'
7.grammar: A noun with the first-person singular possessive pronoun 'my,' which here appears in the fuller form -iya (the connecting vowel -i plus -ya). This -iya ('my') marks possession regardless of the noun's grammatical role in the sentence.
7.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, dwell; a house

8.meaning: An active participle / noun meaning 'a believer' — one who has faith, who trusts and affirms; literally 'one who makes/declares secure' and so gives and receives faith and trust.
8.grammar: Active participle (form IV) used as a noun, masculine singular, indefinite. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative: it marks 'a believer' as the object of a verb, or fills roles such as a specified state or circumstance.

9.meaning: Believers — those who have faith, who inwardly affirm and trust in Allah and give security through that faith; the ones characterized by true belief.
9.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle ('those who believe'), built on the causative Form IV pattern (faith that brings about inner security/affirmation). The plural ending -īna is the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition; here it follows li- ('for'), and the prefixed al- ('the') makes it definite — 'and for the believers.'

10.meaning: And the believing women — the feminine plural of those who have faith, who place their trust and security in Allah and inwardly affirm the truth.
10.grammar: An active participle (one who believes) in the sound feminine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -āti is the sound feminine plural marker in its genitive or accusative form (the -i vowel rather than -u): it names a group of females and signals that the word is governed by a preceding preposition, oath, or verb, or is linked to a following noun.
10.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: You increase / add to. The verb means to give more of something, to augment or add on to what is already there.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking "you" (or a feminine "she") as the doer. Its mood is the jussive — the clipped form used after negating and prohibiting particles — whose stem normally ends in a vowelless consonant. The -i written and heard at the end is not a case or mood ending at all: it is a helping vowel supplied so that the vowelless final consonant does not collide with a consonant cluster beginning the next word.
12.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, add, grow more

13.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
13.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: Utter ruin, destruction, being broken to pieces and brought to nothing. It is the verbal noun naming the act or state of annihilation itself — loss and perdition rather than a mere setback.
15.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) — the naming-word for an action, like English 'destruction' beside 'destroy'. The final '-an' shows two things: the doubled vowel sign (tanwīn) marks it indefinite, and the 'a' vowel is the accusative case, the ending used when the noun is the object of a verb, or is used adverbially to say in what manner or to what outcome something happens.
15.root: ت-ب-ر (t-b-r) — breaking to pieces, ruin, annihilation
